entries.sanskrit: ततः सप्तदशे जन्म तयोर् लोक-भयङ्-करम् । हिरण्याक्ष-प्रभावश् च वर्ण्यते दिग्-जयेऽद्भुतः ॥ क्षेमं विधास्यति \[३.१६.३७\] इति ब्रह्म-वचनानन्तरं । शङ्कया त्यक्ताः ॥१॥
word_for_word: ततः सप्तदशे जन्म तयोर् लोक-भयङ्-करम् । हिरण्याक्ष-प्रभावश् च वर्ण्यते दिग्-जयेऽद्भुतः ॥ क्षेमं विधास्यति \[३.१६.३७\] इति ब्रह्म-वचनानन्तरं । शङ्कया त्यक्ताः ॥१॥

Thereafter the seventeenth chapter describes the birth of the two sons, terrifying to the world, and the astonishing conquest of the directions by Hiraṇyākṣa. After Brahmā’s statement that he would grant their welfare, they were abandoned out of fear.
entries.literal_english: Thereafter the seventeenth chapter describes the birth of the two sons, terrifying to the world, and the astonishing conquest of the directions by Hiraṇyākṣa. After Brahmā’s statement that he would grant their welfare, they were abandoned out of fear.

entries.sanskrit: भर्तुर् आदेशात् \"लोकान् क्रन्दयिष्यति\" इति तद्-वाक्यात् अपत्याभ्यां सर्व-लोकोपद्रवम् अपत्यं प्रति विष्णु-हस्ततो वधाद् वा शङ्कमाना ॥२॥
word_for_word: भर्तुर् आदेशात् \"लोकान् क्रन्दयिष्यति\" इति तद्-वाक्यात् अपत्याभ्यां सर्व-लोकोपद्रवम् अपत्यं प्रति विष्णु-हस्ततो वधाद् वा शङ्कमाना ॥२॥
Because of the husband’s prediction, “He will make the worlds cry,” they feared that the two sons would trouble the entire world; they also feared their being killed by Viṣṇu’s hand.
entries.literal_english: Because of the husband’s prediction, “He will make the worlds cry,” they feared that the two sons would trouble the entire world; they also feared their being killed by Viṣṇu’s hand.

entries.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वेति । ब्रह्म-पुत्रान् सनकादीन् ऋते ब्रह्म-सृष्टाः । सर्वा एव प्रजा अतत्-तत्त्व-विदो भीता विश्व-सम्प्लवं मेनिरे । देवास् तु ब्रह्म-वाक्यात् तत्त्व-विदोऽभीता आसन्, न तु विश्व-सम्प्लवं मेनिरे इत्य् अर्थः ॥१५॥
word_for_word: दृष्ट्वेति । ब्रह्म-पुत्रान् सनकादीन् ऋते ब्रह्म-सृष्टाः । सर्वा एव प्रजा अतत्-तत्त्व-विदो भीता विश्व-सम्प्लवं मेनिरे । देवास् तु ब्रह्म-वाक्यात् तत्त्व-विदोऽभीता आसन्, न तु विश्व-सम्प्लवं मेनिरे इत्य् अर्थः ॥१५॥

Except for Brahmā’s sons, Sanaka and the others, all the creatures born from Brahmā, not knowing the truth, were afraid and thought that the universe was about to dissolve. The gods, knowing the truth because of Brahmā’s word, were fearless and did not think the universe would dissolve.
entries.literal_english: Except for Brahmā’s sons, Sanaka and the others, all the creatures born from Brahmā, not knowing the truth, were afraid and thought that the universe was about to dissolve. The gods, knowing the truth because of Brahmā’s word, were fearless and did not think the universe would dissolve.

entries.sanskrit: ताव् इति । अत्रानयोर् अणिमादि-शक्त्या गूढ-स्थितौ टीका-सम्मतिश् च ॥१६॥
word_for_word: ताव् इति । अत्रानयोर् अणिमादि-शक्त्या गूढ-स्थितौ टीका-सम्मतिश् च ॥१६॥
The word “those two” is explained. The accepted gloss is that they remained hidden here through powers such as aṇimā.
entries.literal_english: The word “those two” is explained. The accepted gloss is that they remained hidden here through powers such as aṇimā.
